prompt: Why does this course quote no Azure price as Azure's?
hint: Lesson 1 says where its prices would have come from.

choices.text: Azure does not publish its prices to anyone without a subscription
choices.why: The Retail Prices API is public and needs no account.

choices.text: The recording machine could not reach the public price list
choices.why: Right. The arithmetic uses round illustrative numbers, and `prices.py` reads the real ones on your computer.

choices.text: Prices differ per customer, so no single number would be true
choices.why: The list price is the same for everybody; discounts come on top of it.

choices.text: Brazilian prices are only published in reais
choices.why: The API answers in US dollars by default, for every region.

prompt: Six of the services this course teaches have no emulator at all. Which are they?
hint: Think of the services whose subject is a platform, not a protocol.

choices.text: Blob Storage, ADLS Gen2, the access tiers and the life-cycle rules
choices.why: Azurite answers Blob Storage; only the Data Lake endpoint is missing.

choices.text: Azure SQL, Managed Instance and the PostgreSQL and MySQL flexible servers
choices.why: The engines run in containers; what is missing is the management around them.

choices.text: Synapse, Fabric, Data Factory, Databricks, Stream Analytics and Purview
choices.why: Right. Those are taught from Microsoft's documentation, and the lessons say so.

choices.text: Cosmos DB and Event Hubs
choices.why: Both have Microsoft emulators, used from lesson 11 and lesson 22.

prompt: What does `AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING="UseDevelopmentStorage=true"` tell the `az storage` commands?
hint: It is a short name the Azure libraries expand.

choices.text: To log in to the subscription stored in `~/.azure`
choices.why: No command in this course logs in; this variable involves no login.

choices.text: To use Azurite on 127.0.0.1, with its fixed account and published key
choices.why: Right. It expands to `devstoreaccount1` and the well-known key, on ports 10000 to 10002.

choices.text: To create a development storage account in `brazilsouth`
choices.why: Nothing creates accounts here; that is the control plane, which no emulator answers.

choices.text: To skip authentication on every request
choices.why: Requests are still signed, with Azurite's published key.

prompt: Put the steps of a sitting of this course in order.
hint: The emulators have to answer before anything asks them.
items: Start the emulators the lesson names with `docker compose up -d` in `~/azure`
Run the four lines of "Every time you open a terminal"
Check that the empty container list comes back without an error
Run the lesson's commands, which rebuild what it needs

prompt: Why is the Blob Storage library pinned to 12.30.0 rather than the newest release?
hint: Each release speaks a protocol version.

choices.text: The newest release dropped support for the Python 3.12 that Ubuntu ships
choices.why: That is not the reason the lesson gives.

choices.text: Azurite 3.37.0 refuses the protocol version newer releases ask for
choices.why: Right. Version 12.30.0 speaks `2026-06-06`, the newest Azurite 3.37.0 understands.

choices.text: The newest release needs an Azure login before it will start at all
choices.why: The library does not log in by itself; it uses the connection string.

choices.text: Microsoft withdrew the newer release
choices.why: It is published; it just speaks a protocol version too new for this Azurite.

prompt: Match each message to its cause.
hint: Read which program could have printed each one.

pairs.right: `~/.local/bin` is not on the path in this terminal

pairs.left: `Please provide storage account name or connection string.`
pairs.right: The connection string was not exported in this terminal

pairs.left: `failed to bind host port 127.0.0.1:10000/tcp: address already in use`

right_distractors: The container name has a capital letter

prompt: An answer in your terminal names a storage account called `stanaprod`. What should you do first?
hint: Azurite's account always has the same name.

choices.text: Nothing; Azurite names its account after the user
choices.why: Azurite's account is always `devstoreaccount1`.

choices.text: Restart Azurite, which picked up a stale name
choices.why: Azurite cannot invent another account name.

choices.text: Stop, and run `az logout`: that command reached a real subscription
choices.why: Right. A login remembered from earlier use of the command line is the only way to get there.

choices.text: Export the connection string again in this terminal and repeat the command
choices.why: The command already reached something that is not Azurite; find out why first.

prompt: What does no emulator in this course answer?
hint: The layer above every service.

choices.text: The data plane of Blob Storage: containers, blobs and their tiers
choices.why: Azurite answers it.

choices.text: Queries over Cosmos DB documents
choices.why: The Cosmos DB emulator runs them.

choices.text: Azure Resource Manager: subscriptions, accounts, roles and bills
choices.why: Right. That is the control plane, and nothing outside Azure answers it.

choices.text: T-SQL, run against a database engine in a container
choices.why: SQL Server runs it in a container.

prompt: `ru.py` reports a request charge of 1 for a write and 1 for a query across every partition. What does that show?
hint: The number has to come from somewhere.

choices.text: The two operations cost the same on Azure
choices.why: On Azure the charge follows the work done; a query across partitions does more of it.

choices.text: The emulator reports a placeholder rather than a measurement
choices.why: Right. Lesson 13 teaches request units from the documentation for that reason.

choices.text: The container was created with too little throughput for the query
choices.why: Throughput limits how many units a second you may spend, not what an operation costs.

choices.text: The query used the partition key after all
choices.why: It filtered on `totalCents` and asked for a cross-partition query.

prompt: Which of these does a success on the emulators prove? Choose all that apply.
hint: The rule at the end of the section.

choices.text: The command is well formed
choices.why: Yes; a malformed request is refused by the emulator too.

choices.text: The program uses the library correctly
choices.why: Yes; the same library talks to Azure with a different connection string.

choices.text: Azure would charge what the emulator reported
choices.why: The emulators leave cost out on purpose.

choices.text: Azure would answer as quickly
choices.why: Archive rehydration is instant on Azurite and takes hours on Azure.

choices.text: Your role would allow it on a real subscription
choices.why: Roles are the control plane; nothing here checks them.

prompt: An operations line in the sheet is priced per `10K`. You expect 2,500,000 such operations a month. By what do you multiply its price?
hint: Read the unit before the price.

choices.why: That would charge each operation the price of ten thousand.
Right: 2,500,000 divided by 10,000.
That divides by a thousand, not ten thousand.
That divides by a hundred thousand.

prompt: Which date should a price be quoted with?
hint: It is the last column the sheet prints.

choices.text: The date you ran the program and read the price
choices.why: That says when you read it, not when it began to apply.

choices.text: The first day of the month in which you read it
choices.why: Prices do not change on a monthly calendar.

choices.text: The date it took effect, `effectiveStartDate`
choices.why: Right. It is in every item the API returns.

choices.text: The date of your subscription's next invoice, when it is charged
choices.why: There is no subscription in this course.

prompt: Which kind of storage account does this course mean whenever it says "storage account"?
hint: General purpose, second version.

choices.text: `BlobStorage`
choices.why: A legacy kind Microsoft retires.

choices.text: `StorageV2`
choices.why: Right. It offers every tier, every replication option and the hierarchical namespace.

choices.text: `FileStorage`
choices.why: That holds premium file shares only.

choices.text: `BlockBlobStorage`
choices.why: That is the premium kind for blobs, a separate choice.

prompt: Quitanda's data must stay in Brazil. Which replication options rule that out?
hint: Look at where the paired region of `brazilsouth` is.

choices.text: LRS and ZRS
choices.why: Both keep every copy inside the region.

choices.text: Only RA-GRS, because it makes the copy readable
choices.why: GRS sends the copy abroad whether or not it is readable.

choices.text: GRS, GZRS and their read-access variants
choices.why: Right. Their extra copies go to `southcentralus`, in Texas.

choices.text: None; Azure keeps all copies in the customer's country
choices.why: The geo-redundant options copy to the paired region, which for Brazil South is abroad.

prompt: What can a region-wide disaster cost an account using GRS?
hint: How does the copy reach the paired region?

choices.text: Nothing; every write reaches both regions before it is acknowledged
choices.why: That would be synchronous; geo-replication is not.

choices.text: The last writes that had not yet been copied across
choices.why: Right. Geo-replication is asynchronous, so the newest writes may not have crossed.

choices.text: Every write since the last daily backup
choices.why: Replication is continuous, not a daily copy.

choices.text: All the data, because GRS keeps one copy in each region
choices.why: GRS keeps three copies in each region.

prompt: Azurite has a single account, always present, called ___.
hint: It appears in every URL Azurite answers.

prompt: What can `terraform validate` tell you about a storage account declaration?
hint: It asks Azure nothing.

choices.text: That the name is free across all of Azure
choices.why: Only Azure knows which names are taken.

choices.text: That a value is outside the provider's list
choices.why: Right, such as `ZZRS` for the replication type.

choices.text: That the subscription has quota for one more account
choices.why: That would need a login and a subscription.

choices.text: What the account will cost per month
choices.why: Terraform has no prices.

prompt: Which of these would Azure refuse as a storage account name? Choose all that apply.
hint: 3 to 24 characters, lowercase letters and digits.

choices.text: `st-quitanda-prd`
choices.why: Hyphens are refused in an account name.

choices.text: `stQuitandaPrd`
choices.why: Capital letters are refused.

choices.text: `stquitandadataanalyticsprd`
choices.why: 26 characters; the maximum is 24.

choices.text: `stquitandadataprd`
choices.why: Valid, if nobody has it already.

choices.text: `stquitandalogsdev`
choices.why: Valid too.

prompt: Why does Quitanda leave the region out of its account names?
hint: A name cannot be changed.

choices.text: Azure refuses region codes in names
choices.why: Nothing refuses them; the rule is Quitanda's.

choices.text: The region is already part of the host name
choices.why: The host name carries the account name and the service, not the region.

choices.text: A name that says one region becomes false once the data lives in a second one
choices.why: Right, and the name can never be corrected.

choices.text: Region codes push the name past the 63 characters a name may have
choices.why: The limit for an account is 24, and the reason is not length.

prompt: After uploading `exports/2026/10/29/orders.csv` to an empty container, how many objects does the container hold?
hint: The slash is only a character.

choices.text: Five: four folders and a blob
choices.why: The folders are drawn by listing tools; they are not stored.

choices.text: One blob, whose name contains the slashes
choices.why: Right. In an account without a hierarchical namespace there are no folders.

choices.text: Two: the `exports` folder and the blob
choices.why: No folder exists, not even the first.

choices.text: None, until each folder in the path is created first
choices.why: There is nothing to create; the upload succeeded.

prompt: Quitanda wants a new account for application logs in development. Which name follows its convention and Azure's rules?
hint: Type, organisation, workload, environment.

choices.text: `quitanda-logs-dev`
choices.why: Hyphens are refused, and the type prefix is missing.

choices.text: `stquitandalogsdev`
choices.why: Right: `st`, `quitanda`, `logs`, `dev`, 17 lowercase characters.

choices.text: `stquitandalogsdevbrs`
choices.why: Valid for Azure, but the convention leaves the region out.

choices.text: `StQuitandaLogsDev`
choices.why: Capital letters are refused.
